title: Retail dip-buying fragility: short a yen cross at the Tokyo open after a five-day decline of at least 1 x ATR20 during which the TFX Click 365 retail open interest grew by 10 or 15 percent or more, against a light-accumulation control (open interest up at most 2 percent on the same decline), holding 2 or 4 weekdays

spec.title: Retail dip-buying fragility: short a yen cross at the Tokyo open after a five-day decline of at least 1 x ATR20 during which the TFX Click 365 retail open interest grew by 10 or 15 percent or more, against a light-accumulation control (open interest up at most 2 percent on the same decline), holding 2 or 4 weekdays
spec.rationale: Mechanism: latent forced supply from an underwater leveraged retail book. Who trades: Japanese retail margin traders, of whom TFX Click 365 is the exchange-traded slice (350,000 to 600,000 open USDJPY contracts in the design years; the OTC margin book is about ten times larger and behaves the same way). They are structurally long the yen crosses for carry and contrarian: they add longs as the crosses fall. Descriptive, design years only: AUDJPY daily open-interest changes correlate -0.26 with daily returns, open interest rises about 3.5 percent on down days and falls 2.2 percent on up days; on five-day declines of at least 1 x ATR20 the five-day open-interest growth has quartiles +4, +9 and +18 percent, so the retail book grows into almost every decline and the question is how much. Why it matters: the positions are 10 to 25 times levered with broker-enforced losscuts, so a book that grew heavily into a decline is latent forced supply: if the decline extends, losscuts fire in a cascade and the move accelerates (the BIS Quarterly Review of December 2019 attributes the 3 January 2019 yen flash crash in large part to Japanese retail losscuts; the August 2015 and January-February 2016 yen-cross drops showed the same pattern), so after heavy accumulation into weakness the return distribution of the cross over the next days is negatively skewed and a short has a positive expectation; after a decline that retail did not buy (the light arm, including days the book shrank, where the losscuts have already happened), there is no latent supply and no continuation is expected, or a bounce. Who is on the other side: real money and CTAs selling the carry, whose selling retail absorbs. The 2011 Bank of Japan Review found that retail margin traders dampen volatility in calm times, which says the expected edge is small outside stress and is why this test pre-registers a one-sided direction (fade the retail accumulation), a monotonicity check (15 percent >= 10 percent >= light) and a modest expectation. What has been measured before: cross_zfade found two-sigma moves on crosses keep running at the daily horizon; fx_volume_climax_reversal found one-day shocks on majors continue and tick volume is not a capitulation signal; trend_follow found price-only trend flat before costs; jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock found no Tokyo-session continuation after a US equity shock and a Tokyo-morning bounce instead, and its mirror long was banned as a snooped flip. None of those had a positioning measure; this test conditions on the retail book itself, has no equity shock, holds for days rather than one session, and carries a control arm (the same decline without accumulation) that isolates the retail-book effect from the plain decline. Costs: AUDJPY spread 0.9 pips, 0.2 pips of slippage each side, 7 dollars commission (about 0.9 pips), about 2.2 pips against a 1.0 x ATR20 stop of 58 to 127 pips (median 81), so about 0.03 R; swap on a short AUDJPY is about -0.4 pips a day in the design years, negligible. Counts (design 2010-2017, from the TFX and price tables, no outcomes): AUDJPY about 460 days with a five-day decline of at least 1 x ATR20 (about 270 at 1.5 x); heavy10 covers about 45 percent of them, heavy15 about 30 percent, light (growth <= 2 percent) about 15 percent; with one position at a time and 2 to 4 weekday holds about 80 to 120 heavy trades and 30 to 45 light trades on AUDJPY; USDJPY, NZDJPY and GBPJPY similar; EURJPY's retail book was not structurally long in 2010-2017 (median five-day open-interest change on declines -2 percent), so it is the natural placebo market and is expected to show the weakest heavy-arm result. Expected: heavy arms +0.08 R, trade-level design t about 1.0 on about 100 trades, light arm at or below zero; P(design t >= 2 | effect real at +0.08 R) about 0.15, so an inconclusive negative is the most likely outcome, but this is the first measurement of the retail-flow dimension and its control fixes the baseline for every later TFX idea. Speed: about 1.1 trades a month per market, about 4 a month pooled over the four structurally long crosses (correlated), score 0.08 x 2 = 0.16: an edge-recording test that reaches the challenge speed bar only at +0.35 R. Human execution: one check of the TFX daily statistics after midnight UTC, one market order at the Tokyo open on the qualifying days, a 1 x ATR20 stop and a time exit two or four weekdays later at 20:30 UTC; a few orders a month. Most likely failure: the accumulation is the normal state of the book, so the heavy arms are the decline itself and the light arm is too small to tell; or the fragility shows only in the two or three crash episodes of the design years and dies in the breadth test.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on AUDJPY, applied by the Director from all 12 stage A rows in the trials table (stage 'A') even if the pipeline reports a candidate: among the 8 heavy cells with at least 40 design trades, the chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t (the pipeline's own ranking); it must have design avg R > 0 and t >= 1; if the automatic floor is cleared only by a 'light' cell, the B/C output is ignored and the hypothesis is scrapped under this rule. (2) Control difference and monotonicity, the test of the mechanism: at the chosen cell, design avg R(heavy) minus design avg R(the light cell with the same k and hold_days) must be >= +0.06 R and the same difference must be > 0 in check; and in design the heavy15 cell at the same k and hold_days must be >= the heavy10 cell minus 0.02 R (more accumulation, more fragility). If the light arm earns as much as the heavy arm, the decline and not the retail book carries the continuation, the lesson is that retail accumulation adds nothing to a plain multi-day decline, and no unconditional follow-the-decline hypothesis may be registered from this run (its sign would be read off the control arm). (3) Breadth: at the chosen cell at least 4 of the 8 design years positive, and design avg R > 0 after dropping the best ceil(N/10) entry dates; a result carried by the 2011, 2015 or 2016 crash months alone is an episode and is recorded as such. (4) Replication: at the chosen cell read from the stage B trials table, the pooled design avg R over NZDJPY, USDJPY and GBPJPY (equal-weighted over trades) must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; EURJPY is the pre-registered placebo (its book was not structurally long in the design years) and is reported, not gated: a EURJPY heavy arm as strong as AUDJPY's is evidence that the signal is the decline, not the book. (5) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands. (6) Pass bar: design t >= 2 at the chosen cell with (2) satisfied in design and check; a positive result below that is recorded as below the bar and is not promoted. Speed: at about 1.1 trades a month per market and +0.08 R the score is 0.16 (about 4 trades a month pooled over the four structurally long crosses), so this is recorded as an edge unless the heavy arm earns +0.35 R or more; honest expectation +0.08 R, design t about 1.0, P(t >= 2 | real) about 0.15; most likely failure: accumulation is the normal state of the book so the heavy arms measure the decline itself, or the fragility lives only in two or three crash episodes.

spec.notes:
All times UTC. H1 bars, stamped at the bar open and sparse; locate every time by timestamp (m.ts for opens, m.close_times() for closes). Loop over TFX rows (about 250 a year), vectorise everything else.

TFX ROWS: t = F.ext_series(m, 'tfx_daily'); keep rows with symbol == m.sym (the price-store symbol column; raise if none) in ts_avail order (ts_avail = Click 365 trading date + 1 day at 00:00 UTC). For row r (TFX date d_r): oi_g_r = oi_r / oi_(r-5) - 1 over the previous five TFX rows (oi_lookback 5); undefined when fewer than five earlier rows exist or any of the six oi values is <= 0.

PRICE CONDITION, from the store's own daily bars: daily = F.daily_bars(m) (trading days closing 17:00 New York); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, atr_n = 20)), known at the day start. At the signal bar (below) the last completed trading day is D (the trading day before the one containing the signal bar). Require daily.date[D] == d_r (the Click 365 day d_r ends at the New York close of d_r, so the two venues describe the same day; skip the row when they do not match, which happens around holidays that one venue observes). drop_atr = (daily.c[D] - daily.c[D - ret_lookback]) / ATR20[sig] with ret_lookback 5 (five trading days). Condition: drop_atr <= -k (k 1.0 or 1.5). Skip if D - 5 < 0 or ATR20[sig] is not finite or <= 0.

BANDS (p['band']): 'heavy10': oi_g_r >= 0.10; 'heavy15': oi_g_r >= 0.15; 'light': oi_g_r <= 0.02 (the control: the same decline without retail accumulation, including days the book shrank). Raise ValueError on any other value. A row trades only if its band condition and the price condition both hold.

SIGNAL BAR AND ENTRY: T = ts_avail of the row (00:00 UTC). sig = the bar whose close time == T (the 23:00-00:00 UTC bar); if no bar closes exactly at T, use the first bar with close time >= T provided close - T <= max_delay_min (120) minutes and the bar's UTC date equals T's date, else skip (a Friday TFX row has T on Saturday and is always skipped). Short only: entry_short[sig] = True, entry_type[sig] = 0, valid_bars[sig] = 1; the fill is at the open of bar sig + 1 (normally the 00:00 UTC bar, 09:00 Tokyo) on the bid plus slippage. One position at a time: an entry while a position is open is ignored by the executor, so overlapping decline days produce one trade per hold.

STOP: sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[sig] (sl_atr 1.0, price units, > 0). tp_dist NaN (no target), max_bars 0.

EXIT: exit date E = the hold_days-th weekday (Monday to Friday) after the UTC date of bar sig + 1 (hold_days 2 or 4; weekends skipped, holidays not); target = E at exit_utc (20:30). xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, E, 20, 30); if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1: exit_short[xi - 1] = True (close at the open of the first bar at or after the target). Causal fallback: for each signalled row k set exit_short True on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= sig_(k+1) (the signal bar of the next signalled row, or m.n - 1 for the last), so a missing target bar closes the position at the first bar after the gap and never carries it into the next trade; a marker on sig_(k+1) acts at the open of the next fill bar, where the executor checks only the stop. Leftover guard: exit_short[sig_k] = True. Markers with no open position are ignored. No other exits, no other filters.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): band (grid 'heavy10', 'heavy15', 'light'), k (grid 1.0, 1.5), hold_days (grid 2, 4); fixed sl_atr 1.0, oi_lookback 5, ret_lookback 5, exit_utc '20:30', max_delay_min 120, atr_n 20. Module GRID = the full 12 cells so the checker exercises every value. Spec grids: stage A on AUDJPY runs all 12 cells (the 'light' cells are the control arm and run only there); stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run band in ('heavy10', 'heavy15') only (8 cells). The Director sets specs/auto/jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility.json after the review step so that stage_a.grid holds the 12 cells and grid holds the two heavy bands.

EXPECTED COUNTS (AUDJPY design 2010-2017, from the TFX and daily tables, a check for the Builder and the checker): about 460 qualifying decline days at k 1.0 (about 270 at 1.5) before the band split and the overlap skips; heavy10 about 45 percent of them, heavy15 about 30 percent, light about 15 percent; about 80 to 120 heavy trades and 30 to 45 light trades after the one-position-at-a-time rule. A count far from these means the symbol subset, the day alignment or the open-interest ratio is wrong.

REPORTING (from the trades; all 12 stage A rows read from the trials table, stage 'A'): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, by-year avg R, mean fill spread in pips and as a share of the stop, for design and for check; for the chosen heavy cell: the matching light cell (same k and hold_days) and the other heavy band at the same k and hold_days, the avg R after dropping the best ceil(N/10) entry dates, the avg R of entries inside the three largest drawdown months of the design years against the rest, and the per-year heavy-minus-light difference in design and check.

PRE-REGISTRATION AMENDMENT (cycle 9, before any run): the Critic revisions R1-R8 in runs/cycles/cycle_0009/critic_review.json are binding (planned-hold de-overlap, Friday rows trade at the Monday 00:00 UTC open, within-strata pooled mechanism gate, tail-only lesson rule); gated markets narrowed to AUDJPY and NZDJPY, where the dip-buying signature holds in every year 2010-2023; USDJPY, GBPJPY and EURJPY are report-only; details in runs/jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility/revision.md.
